clue.text: As a cake may be the morning after St Andrew's Day, thrown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, thrown up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.words: the morning after St Andrew's Day
parts.note: St Andrew's Day is 30 November, so the day after is 1 December, written DEC I with a Roman one

explanation.surface: A baker's note on how a cake might look after a Scottish saint's-day celebration, with an unhappy hint of a hangover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown up' looks like the after-effect of a St Andrew's Day party, but in this down clue it turns DEC I upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake with a sugar coating on top is described as having been given that frosting.

clue.text: Native American tribe in Idaho, Piscataway

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, across the comma

explanation.surface: A Native American people located in Idaho and among the Piscataway of Maryland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Piscataway are a real tribe, which tempts the solver to take that word as the answer; the tribe wanted spans the end of Idaho and the start of Piscataway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Pueblo people of northeastern Arizona, one of the Native American nations.

clue.text: Picked up incorrectly, stray is harmed

indicators.note: stray means wandering off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone misunderstands a message and wrongly hears that a stray animal has been hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up speech is to catch it by ear, so picking it up incorrectly is getting the words wrong when listening.

clue.text: Daring, in the manner of one stripping down?

definitions.meaning: brave and spirited, ready to take risks

definitions.text: in the manner of one stripping down?
definitions.meaning: read as an adjective from pluck, like someone pulling the soft feathers off a bird

explanation.surface: Is a striptease artist brave, behaving as someone who takes it all off?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like the direction of undressing, but it means the fine feathers a poultry plucker strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing pluck, meaning courage and spirit, is the everyday sense of being bold and daring.

clue.text: Every second in bother? Time to begin operation

parts.note: every second letter of the word bother gives O, H and R; the O is read as the figure nought and HR as the abbreviation for an hour

explanation.surface: A frazzled planner fretting over every second before a military operation starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every second letter of 'bother' (b-O-t-H-e-R) to get OHR, then read the O as the digit 0 and HR as the short form of hour.
explanation.definitionFit: In military planning the moment set for an attack or operation to start is called by this phrase.

clue.text: Muddle a hundred Ptolemaic forms

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: forms is read as a verb: the letters of the following word form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scholar bewildered by a hundred versions of the old Ptolemaic system of the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle a matter is to make it more confused and harder to follow, a synonym of the verb here.

clue.text: Rate two persons high, as very tall twins

indicators.note: high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to rank two people highly, as if they were towering twins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' seems to describe the rating, but it is the anagram signal, in the sense of drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair of skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur, once the world's tallest buildings, are identical twin towers.

clue.text: Move to Africa, then Leatherhead!

indicators.note: move as an instruction to shift these letters around into a new order

parts.note: read as Leather head, the head or first letter of leather

explanation.surface: Relocation advice: go to Africa, and then on to Leatherhead, a town in Surrey, England.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark looks like mere punctuation, but in mathematics it is the symbol for this product, so it serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the exclamation mark after a number denotes the product of all positive integers up to it, as in 5! = 120.

clue.text: Satisfied second crew leading with total enthusiasm and energy

parts.note: satisfied after eating means full
a crew is a team working together
leading means in front, ahead

explanation.surface: A contented team captain describes leading a crew with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken from steam engines at maximum power, the idiom means proceeding with all possible vigour.

clue.text: 19 Down east, north or south, going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means read from right to left

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
either end of the earth's axis is a pole

explanation.surface: Directions for a fugitive: whether east, north or south, end up heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: Running off with a lover to marry in secret is to make a getaway, the sense of the cross-referenced phrase.

clue.text: Juvenile, as old player Alan?

parts.note: Alan Ladd was a Hollywood film actor of the 1940s and 1950s
the suffix -ish means like or in the manner of, so it plays the part of as

explanation.surface: Was the film actor Alan Ladd childish in his behaviour?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'like Ladd': Ladd plus the suffix meaning like.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous, immature behaviour typical of young men is described with this adjective, so juvenile in attitude.

clue.text: Hatchet Henry arrested?

definitions.meaning: cryptically, H (the symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance) held inside a copper, a policeman making an arrest

explanation.surface: Someone named Henry was arrested, apparently carrying an axe.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint, not a plain definition: H for Henry held by an unnamed copper, which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A small axe for one hand is a synonym for a short chopping tool, a cleaver or hatchet.

clue.text: Behind Spanish car

definitions.meaning: a carmaker from Spain, part of the Volkswagen group

explanation.surface: A person's rear end, or a motor made in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat is both one's bottom and the name of a Spanish car brand.

clue.text: A payment in use, on the face of it

indicators.note: in says the payment sits inside the word for use

parts.note: to apply something is to put it to use
rent is a regular payment for a property

explanation.surface: A payment made in use, judging by appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean seemingly, judging only by what appears to be the case.

clue.text: Northern Ireland overwhelmed by tiny advance of ancient civilisation

parts.note: baby as an adjective means very small

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swallowed up within the following word

parts.note: an advance of money is a loan

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland swamped by the slight progress of an old civilisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was a great city of ancient Mesopotamia, so the adjective describes that early civilisation.

clue.text: Bare, stealing kiss, so deep in trouble

indicators.note: stealing means taking something in, so the jumbled letters take the kiss inside
in trouble means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the conventional letter for a kiss

explanation.surface: Caught out and laid bare after stealing a kiss, someone is now in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' rearranges SO DEEP, and 'stealing' has that jumble take in X.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something uncovered and unprotected, open to view.

clue.text: US store raised deposit for large plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: Macy's is a famous American department store
ore is a mineral deposit

explanation.surface: An American shop raising a deposit to buy a big plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reads MACYS upwards to give SYCAM.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large tree, a maple in Britain and a plane in America, so an example of a big plant.

clue.text: Better going through Odessa, Prussians in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the hidden letters are read backwards
going through says the letters run through the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Prussian soldiers retreating through Odessa, and doing better for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'Better going through' as the definition, but the answer means only 'Better'; 'going through' signals the hidden letters, which 'in retreat' then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To better a rival is to outdo or exceed them, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Sport spent a penny investing in power

indicators.note: investing in means wrapping or going into, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: sway is power or influence
to spend a penny is a British euphemism for urinating, from the old penny coin for public toilets

explanation.surface: A sport in which someone spent money investing in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent a penny' is British slang for using the toilet, as public toilets once cost a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorcycle racing on short oval dirt tracks is a sport known by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Governor finding currency framework hit hard in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the yen is the Japanese currency
a rack is a framework for holding things
to ram is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A central banker finds the currency system badly hit during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recession' looks like economics but it turns YENRACKRAM backwards. Mark Carney was Governor of the Bank of England from 2013 to 2020.
explanation.definitionFit: He headed the Bank of England, the UK's central bank, whose chief officer has this title.

clue.text: Trump buries negative comment in final electoral challenge

indicators.note: buries means hides inside, so one word is put inside the other

parts.note: in bridge, to ruff is to play a trump card
no is a negative reply

explanation.surface: Donald Trump stifling criticism during a deciding election contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' reads as the politician, but it is the card-game verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A deciding vote between the top two candidates after an inconclusive first round has this name.

clue.text: March the first for David and Punk

indicators.note: the first for means the first letter of the following name

parts.note: emo is a style of rock music that grew out of punk

explanation.surface: A first protest for David alongside the puzzle's setter, Punk.
explanation.walkthrough: Punk is this puzzle's setter, which tempts a reading of ME; instead it stands for the punk offshoot emo.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is a demonstration, often shortened to this word.

clue.text: A game where drawing may lead to defeat?

definitions.text: A game where drawing may lead to defeat?

parts.words: A game where drawing may lead to defeat?
parts.note: in this word-guessing game each wrong guess adds a line to a gallows drawing, and finishing the picture means losing

explanation.surface: A sporting puzzle: a game in which a draw could somehow lose you the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawing sounds like a tied result, but it means sketching the gibbet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the pencil-and-paper guessing game, a completed sketch of a figure on gallows means the guesser has lost.

clue.text: One after the other, keys let down

definitions.meaning: three musical keys in sequence up the scale: D, then E flat, then E
to release the air from a tyre or balloon

explanation.surface: Someone pressing the keys in order, only to be left disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: The keys are musical: D, E flat and E, one after the other up the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a tyre or balloon is to release the air from it, the literal sense of the verb.

clue.text: Touched cloth

definitions.meaning: past tense of feel: handled or sensed by contact

explanation.surface: Fingering a piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of feeling something and a pressed woollen fabric.

clue.text: Almost wrong, authors' name

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: amiss means wrong or faulty

explanation.surface: Writers have nearly got their own name wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis and his son Martin are both novelists, hence the plural 'authors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley and his son Martin, both British novelists, share this surname.

clue.text: More accomplished Ibsen role needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title role of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: A more skilled actor in an Ibsen role so famous it needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' sounds like praise for a celebrated part, but it drops the G of GABLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of able, meaning more skilled or capable.

clue.text: More than one weakness is a trifle embarrassing

indicators.note: embarrassing in the sense of throwing into disorder, so these letters are confused

explanation.surface: Having several weaknesses is a little bit embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of frailty, a weakness or failing, so several such flaws.
